Gran Turismo 7 Will Let You Drive a 1954 Maserati Spyder for Free for Two Weeks
21 photos
Photo: autoevolution
I’m currently experiencing some unexpected back pain which means I can’t really get out of bed. Luckily for me, both the TV and PS5 are in my bedroom and today Gran Turismo 7 has a new Online Time Trial for us to go through. It’s nice being able to play and work without having to sit at a desk.
I didn’t get any reward from the Time Trial that concluded today, and I honestly even forgot what it was. Once I saw the photo of the Xiaomi Vision Gran Turismo I realized what had happened.
I’m frankly upset Polyphony chose this car for the first ever Time Trial at Sugo, where any Japanese car in the game would have been the perfect match. I didn’t even buy his VGT, despite the Seasonal Menu and 5-Star Roulette Ticket reward available for it.
While I’ve almost accepted the idea that electrification is here to stay in the real world, I won’t accept it being shoved down my throat in the virtual realm.
If you feel the same way, you’ll be happy to know that the car we can drive for free for the next two weeks is a classic racer from the 1950s that’s typically worth almost three million credits! But first, I needed to warm up!
McLaren F1 GTR - BMW '95 Photo: autoevolution I paid 20 million credits for the McLaren F1 GTR -BMW ‘95 last week and I intend to get my money’s worth by driving it around every single circuit in the game. It’s by no means a purely financial decision, as it’s exhilarating to drive despite being 30+ years old.
It was fast enough for a 6:44 lap of the Nurburgring Nordschleife last week, and I’m curious to see how much I can improve after 20 to 30 more attempts. Anyway, I didn’t change a single thing about it for today’s time attack session.
In hindsight, it’s not the perfect idea for the first lap of the day especially since I’m not that familiar with Blue Moon Speedway’s Infield A layout. Experiencing this combo further reassures me that GT7 is a much better game than NASCAR 26 , and I challenge anyone who thinks otherwise to at least play both before making up their mind on the topic.
I lapped Infield A in 71 seconds on my second attempt, and I’m certain someone who’s more experienced can get a lot closer to the one minute marker.
Caterham Seven Superlight R500 '08 Photo: autoevolution Going from 600 bhp to just 63 bhp might seem a bit extreme, until you realize the Caterham Seven Superlight R500 weighs less than half of what the McLaren does.
That’s also partly due to the fact that the one I used today doesn’t have the original engine anymore. And I feared it might feel painfully slow down the acceleration zones of the fictional tri-oval venue.
It obviously topped out at 93 mph/150 kph, but even at that point there’s still a much better sense of speed in GT7 than you get in NASCAR 26 at 150 mph (241 kph).
Anyway, less is sometimes more, and you’ll forget about the slow straight sections once you hit the corners! I’d say this car is an excellent choice for someone who’s still in his early days of sim racing and needs to ease into it.
Ford Mustang 2015 American Racer Photo: autoevolution While a lap in the Caterham took me one minute and 40 seconds, I knew the Ford Mustang Racer would be considerably faster with 800 bhp on tap. That’s about what you’d expect from a 2026 NASCAR racer.
I couldn’t just train at this venue without using some good old American muscle, right? I went with a Cheez-it livery for the job, and soon found myself storming down the main straight at 186 mph (300 kph).
The power delivery on this thing is formidable to say the least, but the handling is not quite on par. Well, that could just be a side-effect of having driven the McLaren first, as that’s in a different league altogether.
I messed up on three different laps, either braking too late or accelerating too early out of a corner. My fastest lap was only three seconds slower than the one in the F1 GTR, and now I’m curious to see what the outcome would be if the two would go up against each other on a regular oval layout.
Ford Mustang Mach 1 '71 Photo: autoevolution Have you seen my recent Hot Wheels unboxing ? I opened a Ford Mustang Mach 1 that first showed up in toy stores in 1998, and it was easily one of my favorites out of the 10 items I took photos of.
It reminded me that I hadn’t driven my virtual ‘71 Mach 1 in a long time so that’s what I wanted to do today.
Do yourself a favor and find a solution to replace the factory-spec four-speed gearbox before any high-speed run, though.
I’m currently at 464 bhp with my supercharged setup, and it felt slightly underpowered after the Mustang American Racer. I also had to deal with some wheelspin in third gear, but it was ultimately more user-friendly if that’s what you’re looking for.
Time Trial Photo: autoevolution When I signed in today, the Time Trial had only been available for 24 minutes. Calster was already up in P1 with a 1:20.730 fast lap, while holl01 was in P2 (0.4 seconds behind). At the time of writing, over 7,000 people have signed up for the event, and only 1% of them are faster than 1:22.000. Meanwhile, the slowest (reasonable) lap time is 1:42.629.
That player needs to improve by at least 14 seconds if he plans on scoring the Bronze Record Reward! The target for Gold is quite a bit more challenging at 1:23.151, and it won’t get any easier from here. Let’s focus on the car we’ll be driving for a moment. The 1,986cc engine in this Maserati uses a rather unusual inline-six cylinder setup, with a maximum output of 166 bhp.
If you like oldschool Ferraris, you’ve certainly heard of the man who built the engine: Gioacchino Colombo. We’re obviously talking about an FR layout here, and the car weighs just 1,631 lbs (740 kg). The gearing is pretty unusual if you’re used to modern cars, as third will go all the way up to 124 mph (200 kph).
That said, don’t be afraid to use first gear in some of the tighter corners at Blue Moon Speedway, or else you’ll find yourself too low in the rev-range. Understeer can be a problem at times as I soon discovered, but other than this Maserati is plenty of fun. I secured a Bronze Record Reward after just three laps, and I might go at it again using the Logitech RS50 and the PS VR2 combo for maximum immersion.

About the author: Dragos Chitulescu
The things Dragos enjoys the most in life are, in no particular order: cars, motorcycles, diecast cars, and drifting.
